findings.title: Port Collision Risk Due to Overlapping Seat Data
findings.explanation: The code in city-spawn-claude.js attempts to avoid port collisions by tracking used ports from seat-map.json. However, the seat-map.json file shows overlapping ports (e.g., seat-1 and seat-16 both use port 9223). The script assumes unique ports when calculating the next available port, but since it only tracks ports within a single execution, it does not prevent reuse of already assigned ports across multiple runs. This will lead to EADDRINUSE errors if a new agent is spawned on a port already in use by an existing process.
findings.fix: Modify the port selection logic to cross-check against all existing ports in seat-map.json across runs and ensure no duplicates are assigned, even if a port appears 'free' during a single execution. Persist a global port reservation list or implement a port cleanup mechanism for stale entries.

findings.title: Inefficient Port Scanning Logic
findings.explanation: The findFreePort function iterates through ports sequentially until it finds a free one, which can be slow if many ports are in use or if the starting port is far from an available one. While this doesn't break functionality, it introduces unnecessary latency in high-contention scenarios.
findings.fix: Optimize port selection by implementing a randomized or binary search approach for port scanning, or maintain a cached list of recently found free ports to start from.

findings.title: Lock file race condition
findings.explanation: The code attempts to create a lock file using 'wx' mode, which creates the file if it doesn't exist or truncates it if it does. However, if another process acquires the lock between the fs.statSync check and the fs.writeFileSync call, the lock file may already exist, causing the function to fail. This can lead to deadlocks or lost seat allocations.
findings.fix: Use fs.openSync with 'wx' mode instead of fs.writeFileSync. This ensures the file is opened exclusively and will fail immediately if the lock is held, allowing the caller to retry or handle the error appropriately.

findings.title: Port calculation can fail when all seats have null ports
findings.explanation: When usedPorts is empty (all seats have null ports), spreading usedPorts produces no arguments for Math.max, causing NaN. This breaks port allocation logic.
findings.fix: Add null check: const highestUsedPtyPort = usedPorts.size > 0 ? Math.max(9300, ...usedPorts) : 9300;

findings.title: Race condition in child process error handling
findings.explanation: The async error handler creates a race where the main process might exit before the rollback completes, leaving the seat map in an inconsistent state.
findings.fix: Move rollback logic to a synchronous function and call it directly in the error handler before process.exit.

findings.title: Port collision with existing seats
findings.explanation: seat-1 has pty_port:9301 and port:9223, seat-16 has port:9223 and pty_port:9302. usedPorts collects both port and pty_port values. Math.max(9300, 9223, 9301, 9302, ...) returns 9302. findFreePort(9303) finds next available >=9303 for ptyPort. Then highestUsedVsCodePort = Math.max(9222, 9303, ...) returns >=9303. findFreePort(>=9304) assigns vsCodePort >=9304. But existing seats expect VS Code debug ports ~922x (9223-9229 used). New seat gets vscode port 9304+ which likely fails VS Code debug protocol integration since spawned pty-claude.js probably assumes standard VS Code port range.
findings.fix: Separate port collections: const usedPtyPorts = new Set(); const usedVsCodePorts = new Set(); then if(seat.pty_port) usedPtyPorts.add(); if(seat.port) usedVsCodePorts.add(); Use respective sets for findFreePort with proper base ports: ptyPort = await findFreePort(Math.max(9300, ...usedPtyPorts), usedPtyPorts); vsCodePort = await findFreePort(Math.max(9222, ...usedVsCodePorts), usedVsCodePorts);

findings.title: Spawn error rollback lacks atomicity under contention
findings.explanation: child.on('error') triggers async rollback which re-acquires lock. If another city-spawn-claude.js concurrently reads seat-map.json between original releaseLock() and error handler execution, it sees half-written seat (valid port but dead process), increments maxSeatNum past it, writes new seat, releases lock. Rollback then deletes wrong seat (deletes new seat-18 instead of failed seat-17) or fails lock acquisition entirely, leaving ghost seat in seat-map.json that breaks city deliberation/integration.
findings.fix: Don't releaseLock() until child 'spawn success' timeout confirms process alive. Add child.on('spawn', ...) + setTimeout(1000). Use spawn({stdio:'pipe'}) temporarily to detect immediate spawn failure before unref/detach. Only releaseLock() + daemonize after process verification.

findings.title: Log FD leak on normal spawn success
findings.explanation: logFd opened but never closed on success path. spawn uses open FD which remains open in parent process even after child unref(). Minor resource leak, but FD stays valid since logFile 'a' mode.
findings.fix: logFd passed to spawn stdio - add child.on('exit', () => fs.closeSync(logFd)); but since detached this won't fire. Better: spawn with {stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']}, child.stdout.pipe(fs.createWriteStream(logFile,{flags:'a'})). Then process can exit cleanly.

findings.fix: Change the default to `Math.max(9301, ...usedPorts, 0)` to match the first existing PTY port range.

findings.title: Potential crash due to reused port in seat-16 and seat-2
findings.explanation: The `findFreePort` function ensures no reused port within `usedPorts`, but `seat-16` in seat-map.json already uses port 9301, which overlaps with `seat-2`'s `pty_port` (9301). findings.title: Race condition in lock release during spawn failure
findings.explanation: The lock is released immediately after writing the seat map, but before the child process is spawned. If spawn fails, the rollback logic (lines 195-235) attempts to re-acquire the lock, but there's a window where another process could acquire the lock between the initial release and the rollback's re-acquisition. This could lead to seat map corruption or inconsistent state.
findings.fix: Move the releaseLock() call to after the child process is confirmed spawned (after line 245). Only release the lock in the error handler if spawn fails before the child is created.

findings.title: Port collision risk due to incorrect usedPorts tracking
findings.code: usedPorts.add(ptyPort); // Claim it immediately so vsCodePort doesn't reuse it
findings.explanation: The code adds ptyPort to usedPorts before confirming the VS Code port is available. If findFreePort() fails for the VS Code port, the ptyPort remains in usedPorts, but the seat map write will fail, leaving the system in an inconsistent state where the port is marked as used but not actually allocated.
findings.fix: Only add ports to usedPorts after both findFreePort() calls succeed. Move both usedPorts.add() calls after line 154.

findings.title: Inconsistent error handling in lock acquisition
findings.code: throw e; // properly propagate non-EEXIST errors
findings.explanation: The code throws non-EEXIST errors immediately during lock acquisition, but other error types (like EACCES) are caught and ignored in the stat check. This inconsistency could mask permission issues or other filesystem problems.
findings.fix: Standardize error handling by either throwing all filesystem errors or implementing consistent retry logic for all recoverable errors.

findings.title: Potential log file descriptor leak
findings.explanation: The log file descriptor (logFd) is opened but never explicitly closed if the spawn succeeds. While Node.js will eventually clean this up, it's poor practice and could lead to resource exhaustion in long-running processes.
findings.fix: Add a finally block to close logFd after spawn: `finally { if (logFd !== process.stderr.fd) fs.closeSync(logFd); }`

findings.title: Seat map corruption risk during atomic write failure
findings.explanation: If the rename operation fails (e.g., due to filesystem errors), the temporary file remains, and the original seat-map.json is left unchanged. However, the code continues execution assuming the write succeeded, leading to a divergence between the in-memory seatMap and the on-disk state.
findings.fix: Wrap the rename operation in a try-catch and throw an error if it fails. Only proceed with spawn if the rename succeeds.

findings.title: Inconsistent seat ID parsing
findings.explanation: The code assumes all seat IDs follow the 'seat-N' format, but there's no validation. If a seat ID doesn't match this pattern (e.g., 'seat-abc'), parseInt will return NaN, which is ignored in the maxSeatNum calculation, potentially leading to seat ID collisions.
findings.fix: Add validation: `if (!key.startsWith('seat-') || isNaN(num)) continue;`

representative.title: Port Collision Risk Due to Overlapping Seat Data
representative.explanation: The code in city-spawn-claude.js attempts to avoid port collisions by tracking used ports from seat-map.json. However, the seat-map.json file shows overlapping ports (e.g., seat-1 and seat-16 both use port 9223). The script assumes unique ports when calculating the next available port, but since it only tracks ports within a single execution, it does not prevent reuse of already assigned ports across multiple runs. This will lead to EADDRINUSE errors if a new agent is spawned on a port already in use by an existing process.
representative.fix: Modify the port selection logic to cross-check against all existing ports in seat-map.json across runs and ensure no duplicates are assigned, even if a port appears 'free' during a single execution. Persist a global port reservation list or implement a port cleanup mechanism for stale entries.

allFindings.title: Port collision with existing seats
allFindings.explanation: seat-1 has pty_port:9301 and port:9223, seat-16 has port:9223 and pty_port:9302. usedPorts collects both port and pty_port values. allFindings.fix: Separate port collections: const usedPtyPorts = new Set(); const usedVsCodePorts = new Set(); then if(seat.pty_port) usedPtyPorts.add(); if(seat.port) usedVsCodePorts.add(); Use respective sets for findFreePort with proper base ports: ptyPort = await findFreePort(Math.max(9300, ...usedPtyPorts), usedPtyPorts); vsCodePort = await findFreePort(Math.max(9222, ...usedVsCodePorts), usedVsCodePorts);

This could lead to seat map corruption or inconsistent state.
allFindings.fix: Move the releaseLock() call to after the child process is confirmed spawned (after line 245). Only release the lock in the error handler if spawn fails before the child is created.

allFindings.title: Spawn error rollback lacks atomicity under contention
allFindings.explanation: child.on('error') triggers async rollback which re-acquires lock. If another city-spawn-claude.js concurrently reads seat-map.json between original releaseLock() and error handler execution, it sees half-written seat (valid port but dead process), increments maxSeatNum past it, writes new seat, releases lock. Rollback then deletes wrong seat (deletes new seat-18 instead of failed seat-17) or fails lock acquisition entirely, leaving ghost seat in seat-map.json that breaks city deliberation/integration.
allFindings.fix: Don't releaseLock() until child 'spawn success' timeout confirms process alive. Add child.on('spawn', ...) + setTimeout(1000). Use spawn({stdio:'pipe'}) temporarily to detect immediate spawn failure before unref/detach. Only releaseLock() + daemonize after process verification.

representative.title: Log FD leak on normal spawn success
representative.explanation: logFd opened but never closed on success path. spawn uses open FD which remains open in parent process even after child unref(). Minor resource leak, but FD stays valid since logFile 'a' mode.
representative.fix: logFd passed to spawn stdio - add child.on('exit', () => fs.closeSync(logFd)); but since detached this won't fire. Better: spawn with {stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']}, child.stdout.pipe(fs.createWriteStream(logFile,{flags:'a'})). Then process can exit cleanly.
